title: 7-Year Treasury Note auction (November new issue) — the day before Thanksgiving, closing 11:30am ET not 1:00pm
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream by THIS event's initial research — a third independent read of the same primary, after the two sibling proposals this file supersedes. Row reads verbatim `7-Year NOTE Thursday, November 19, 2026 Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Monday, November 30, 2026` with NO trailing `R`; the flag column IS populated elsewhere in the same block (`10-Year TIPS R T`, `2-Year FRN R`, `20-Year BOND R`), so the blank is a positive signal of a new issue, not a missing field. The AUCTION TIME is sourced rather than assumed: fiscaldata auctions_query publishes `closing_time_comp`, which reads `11:30 AM` on all six pre-Thanksgiving 7-Year auctions in the record (2014-11-26, 2015-11-25, 2016-11-23, 2019-11-27, 2024-11-27, 2025-11-26) and on both Christmas-Eve ones (2014-12-24, 2025-12-24) against `01:00 PM` on 143 of the other 144 — so 2026-11-25 should be read as an 11:30am ET close. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-11-19 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read both prior proposals first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/treasury-7y-note-2026-11-25.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23.json and .from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-19.json, now shadowed and inert. Both are carried forward: the same-announcement/same-settlement structure from the 2Y sweep, and the measured early-close time plus the pre-Thanksgiving demand null from the announcement sweep. THE EARLY CLOSE IS A HALF-DAY PHENOMENON, NOT A THANKSGIVING ONE — the correction this research makes to its own proposals: `closing_time_comp` reads 11:30 AM on 9 of 152 auctions since 2014, six pre-Thanksgiving AND two Christmas-Eve (2014-12-24, 2025-12-24), plus one unexplained (2016-02-26, a Friday with no holiday). The mechanism is the SIFMA 2:00pm recommended bond close, and Treasury moves the auction forward by the same 90 minutes the close moves, so the post-auction observation window is 2.5 hours either way — identical, which is why the day is readable at all. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING, and the reason this event earns a full ledger: the ~1bp 7Y-minus-10Y auction-day flattening that treasury-7y-note-2026-10-29.md measured (-0.95bp, t=-5.04) reproduces EXACTLY on its own 2023-01-onward window and REVERSES SIGN out of sample (2014-2021: +0.479bp, t=+3.98, against a flat last-8-business-day calendar control both sides). It is not a constant. It is a linear function of DEALER TAKEDOWN: 7s10s = -1.894 + 0.090 x dealer%, slope t=7.83 over all 152, surviving a linear time-trend control (partial corr +0.349, t=4.55) and year-demeaning (slope +0.082, t=3.83). SIZE EXPECTATION $44B, unchanged at every 7-Year since 2024-04-25 and identical in all six monthly rows sb0590 publishes; the November grid is set at the 2026-11-04 refunding. SESSION CONTEXT: 26 tracked events sit within five days and five share the date (pce-2026-11-25, gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25, durable-goods-2026-11-25, new-home-sales-2026-11-25, beige-book-2026-11-25) because Thanksgiving pulls the slate forward — the most saturated corridor this calendar carries.
